newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian coconut oil falls, demand poor.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian coconut oil falls, demand poor.

text.p: Indonesian coconut oil and copra prices fell on Friday amid continued sluggish consumer demand, traders said.
"Prices continue to fall and I suspect this trend happens because people have switched to olein, which is much cheaper," said one trader in Jakarta.
Traders said coconut oil was quoted at 1,700 rupiah/kg in Jakarta against 1,750 last week. Copra fell to 750 rupiah/kg against last week's price of 800.
They said demand for copra from refineries which processed coconut oil was also slow, hurting market sentiment.
Traders said concern over security ahead of the May 29 general elections had kept some market players on the sidelines. Sporadic violence has marred the election campaign.

They said they expected a more positive trend in the coconut oil market after the election. "We have seen some clashes taking place in several parts of the country and this affects market sentiment," said another trader.

Palm olein was quoted at 1,440-50 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, compared with 1,445-50 rupiah/kg at Thursday's close. Crude palm oil was done at 1,245 and 1,247 rupiah/kg at a tender for two parcels of 500 tonnes each in Medan on Wednesday.

Traders in Manila said on Monday coconut oil prices were expected to continue slipping this week, weighed down by steep falls in soyoil prices in Chicago and prospects of rising copra and alternative oil supplies in the region.
